source_coverage.method: Unique canonical IDs in implemented tailoring or actual additional learner-guide paths. Legacy projections alone do not close this pass. Source coverage is not integration or formal acceptance.

authoring.provenance: Exact projection of the reviewed M4 runtime protocol with additive M6A governance metadata.

legacy_compatibility_exceptions.detail: The frozen M4 action rule names user_initiated, but the runtime check-in vocabulary omits that field.
legacy_compatibility_exceptions.resolution_gate: M6B typed-evidence architecture and any later protocol revision.

meaning_and_fit.purpose: Create and repeat one safe period of play pursued for enjoyment rather than output, optimization, or public performance.
meaning_and_fit.why_recommended: Your current provisional profile identifies playfulness, recreation, and non-instrumental activity as a useful area for practice.

claims.statement: This experiment observes whether one chosen activity can remain non-instrumental; it does not measure creativity, happiness, or a person's worth.
claims.limitations: The migrated five-protocol slice has not been validated as a psychometric instrument or as proof of broad competency change.

meaning_and_fit.applicability_question: Is there a safe, accessible activity you can do primarily for enjoyment rather than productivity or improvement?
meaning_and_fit.not_applicable_behavior: Record not applicable or defer without penalty, do not infer a deficit, and offer the listed safe alternative when useful.
meaning_and_fit.readiness_considerations: Use when a low-stakes activity can be chosen voluntarily without neglecting care, work, safety, recovery, or other current responsibilities.
meaning_and_fit.opportunity_considerations: Requires two realistically available windows and a free or affordable activity that can be adapted to current energy, mobility, and sensory needs.
safe_alternatives: Use a five-minute playful variation of an existing routine when a longer window is unavailable.
Defer without penalty during seasons where rest or essential responsibilities need priority.
role_conditions: Caregivers and shift workers may split the activity into shorter safe windows.
pathway_conditions: Solo, shared, indoor, outdoor, quiet, active, digital, and analog play are all legitimate.
worldview_conditions: The practice does not prescribe one theory of leisure, celebration, or flourishing.

intervention.cadence: Reserve, complete, and revisit one form of play during ten days.
intervention.setup: Choose one low-stakes form of play that is realistically available now. Examples may include a game, making something, movement, music, or playful exploration.
intervention.privacy_and_boundaries: Choose an activity that is physically, financially, and socially safe. Do not use the practice to pressure another person, ignore responsibilities, or turn rest into another performance target.
intervention.expected_burden: About 50–75 minutes total; shorter accessible variants are legitimate.
foreseeable_misuse: Turning play into a compulsory optimization target or using a risky, costly, compulsive, or pressured activity.
exclusions: Gambling, substance use, unsafe physical activity, material financial risk, or neglect of essential care and responsibilities.

actions.title: Reserve a play window
actions.instructions: Choose a specific activity and reserve at least 30 minutes for it within the next three days.

actions.title: Play without an output goal
actions.instructions: Use the reserved time for the activity. For that window, do not optimize, publish, measure, or turn it into work.

actions.title: Return once
actions.instructions: Within seven days, return to the activity for another short period or choose a second playful activity.

low_resource: Use imagination, humor, movement, music, nature, or a free game with materials already available.
accessibility: Choose seated, low-sensory, asynchronous, or assistive-technology-supported play.
cultural_context: Choose forms of play that fit the person's community, privacy, age, and responsibilities.
resource_variants: Shorten or split the play window while keeping it free of an output goal.

pause_conditions: Pause when energy, pain, cost, safety, consent, or essential responsibilities make the chosen window unsuitable.
stop_conditions: Stop if the activity becomes unsafe, compulsive, financially disproportionate, or another performance demand.
escalation_conditions: Use appropriate qualified support when play is entangled with gambling, substance use, injury risk, or severe functional impairment.
professional_referral_conditions: Seek appropriate qualified support for gambling, substance, injury, compulsion, or severe functional-impairment concerns.

adverse_or_contradictory_indicators: The activity created avoidable safety, financial, or responsibility harm.
Another person was pressured to participate.
The activity was converted into output, optimization, or public evaluation.
evidence_and_scoring.independence_rule: Record self-directed, planning-aid, or guided support under GG-EVIDENCE-1.0; support changes evidence mass, not human worth.
evidence_and_scoring.context_transfer_rule: Evidence remains attached to the observed context; one context never establishes broad competency transfer.
evidence_and_scoring.repetition_rule: Repeated observations use the frozen diminishing-return multipliers in GG-EVIDENCE-1.0 and remain independently replayable.
evidence_and_scoring.recency_rule: No new retention mathematics is introduced in M6A; later evidence remains dated and any future recency rule requires a versioned contract.
evidence_and_scoring.performance_rubric: Performance concerns reserving, engaging in, and revisiting the selected activity without an output goal; enjoyment intensity is not scored.
evidence_and_scoring.evidence_quality_rubric: Quality reflects a clear activity, firsthand observations, and distinguishable conditions; free-text enthusiasm does not increase evidence.
evidence_and_scoring.scoring_eligibility: Replay-verified structured evidence is score eligible under the explicit activation ledger; action-specific provenance and withholding rules still apply.
evidence_and_scoring.competency_contribution: The runtime event is evidence about protocol performance only; direct competency state is not implemented in M6A.
evidence_and_scoring.minimum_evidence_before_state_update: One submitted replay-verified event with an observed competency measurement and no applicable withholding condition may update current state; completion alone never does.
withholding_conditions: All evidence is withheld from current score state.
Completion or reported enjoyment does not establish transfer or mastery.
Unsafe, pressured, or materially harmful activity is adverse evidence, not success.

completion_criteria: At least one period of genuinely non-instrumental engagement
completion_and_review.mastery_disclaimer: Completing this practice does not establish mastery.
completion_and_review.progression_criteria: Repeat or vary the activity only when the practice remained safe, voluntary, and realistically compatible with responsibilities.
completion_and_review.transfer_limit: One or two play windows show only what happened in the selected activity and do not establish a stable capacity for leisure or spontaneity.

reflection.before: What would make this activity genuinely playful rather than another task to optimize?
reflection.during: When did output, comparison, or self-evaluation enter the activity, and what helped you return to play?
reflection.after: What made play workable, what constrained it, and did the second window support or contradict the first?

review_guidance.repeat: Repeat a workable low-stakes form of play when it still feels freely chosen.
review_guidance.adapt: Change duration, sensory load, social format, cost, or movement demands.
review_guidance.stop: Stop if the activity becomes unsafe, compulsive, pressured, or another performance obligation.
review_guidance.escalate: Seek appropriate support for gambling, substance, injury, or severe impairment concerns.

evidence_examples.supportive: The user reserved time, played without an output goal, and returned once without creating harm.
evidence_examples.mixed: The activity happened but repeatedly shifted into optimization or could not be revisited.
evidence_examples.contradictory: The activity created pressure, avoidable harm, or displaced essential responsibilities.
evidence_examples.inconclusive: The window was interrupted or too little activity occurred to tell whether it was non-instrumental.
